name: London Sweep Reversal
hypothesis: During the London open (07:00-09:00 UTC bar closes), stops resting beyond the Asian session range (00:00-06:00 UTC) are swept and price closes back inside the range; the subsequent rotation toward the opposite Asian boundary offers asymmetric payoff with the sweep extreme as structural invalidation.
entry_conditions: M15 bar closing 07:00-09:00 UTC whose low undercuts the Asian low by at least 0.05 ATR(14) and closes back above it in the upper half of its range (LONG), symmetric for SHORT; Asian range built from at least 20 M15 bars and not wider than 4 ATR; no earlier sweep of either Asian boundary earlier the same day; planned RR >= 2.
exit_conditions: Fixed stop-loss and take-profit; take-profit at the opposite Asian session boundary; time exit after 18 hours if neither barrier trades.
stop_loss_method: Sweep bar extreme minus/plus 0.15 M15 ATR(14) buffer; risk must be between 0.6 and 5 ATR.
take_profit_method: Opposite Asian range boundary (structural liquidity objective); trade admitted only when (target-entry)/risk >= 2.
risk_model: One planned risk unit per opportunity; one opportunity per symbol per day enforced by model state; per-symbol overlap lock enforced by the common evaluator.
intended_conditions: FX majors, gold and crypto during liquid London hours; regimes where session liquidity pools get swept and retrace (mean-rotating intraday regimes).
limitations: UTC-fixed windows ignore daylight-saving shifts; excludes indices (shared evaluator cannot finance modes 2/3); spread/risk gate 0.1 not always met on wide-spread symbols; small sample sizes per symbol; historical partitions already exposed to prior research.

name: Volatility Exhaustion Fade
hypothesis: When the H1 regime is non-trending (10-bar efficiency ratio <= 0.35), an M15 bar expanding beyond 1.6 ATR on elevated tick volume, closing at its range extreme and exceeding the prior 20-bar extreme after a six-bar run, marks local exhaustion; price then rotates back toward the recent mean.
entry_conditions: M15 range >= 1.6 ATR(14); close in the extreme 20% of the bar; close beyond the prior 20-bar highest high or lowest low; six-bar move >= 1.2 ATR; tick volume >= 1.3x median of prior 20 bars; H1 ER10 <= 0.35; not Friday after 20:00 UTC, not Saturday, not Sunday before 22:00 UTC; planned RR >= 2.
exit_conditions: Fixed stop-loss and take-profit; take-profit at the 12-bar M15 close mean (or 2.2R fallback if the mean is too close); time exit after 24 hours.
stop_loss_method: Climax bar extreme plus/minus 0.15 M15 ATR(14) buffer; risk between 0.6 and 5 ATR.
take_profit_method: Mean of the prior 12 M15 closes; if that yields RR < 2, a 2.2R structural fallback; admitted only when planned RR >= 2.
risk_model: One planned risk unit per opportunity; per-symbol overlap lock enforced by the common evaluator.
intended_conditions: Range-bound or rotating intraday regimes in FX, gold and crypto; avoids trending regimes via the H1 efficiency filter.
limitations: Efficiency-ratio filter is coarse and can admit late-trend climaxes; mean-reversion trades face unbounded tail risk in regime breaks; excludes indices (shared evaluator cannot finance modes 2/3); spread/risk gate 0.1 not always met; historical partitions already exposed to prior research.

name: Opening Range Drive
hypothesis: The first hour of the London session builds an informative opening range; when a later London bar closes beyond a tight version of that range on elevated tick volume, with a decisive body and the last H1 bar aligned, institutional participation drives continuation proportional to the range height.
entry_conditions: Opening range from the four M15 bars 07:00-08:00 UTC, all present, width <= 3 ATR(14) and > 0; trigger M15 closing 08:00-11:00 UTC beyond the range with body >= 0.35 ATR, close in the directional 30% of the bar, tick volume >= 1.4x median of prior 20 bars, and last H1 bar agreeing; no earlier close beyond the range that day; planned 2.5R.
exit_conditions: Fixed stop-loss and take-profit; take-profit at 2.5x planned risk; time exit after 12 hours if neither barrier trades.
stop_loss_method: Opening-range midpoint when that distance is at least 0.6 ATR, else a 0.8 ATR floor stop from the reference close; risk between 0.6 and 5 ATR.
take_profit_method: Entry plus 2.5 times the planned risk in the breakout direction.
risk_model: One planned risk unit per opportunity; one trigger per day enforced by model state; per-symbol overlap lock enforced by the common evaluator.
intended_conditions: FX majors, gold and crypto on London days with a tight opening range and genuine midday participation.
limitations: UTC-fixed windows ignore daylight-saving shifts; false breakouts cluster around news; excludes indices (shared evaluator cannot finance modes 2/3); spread/risk gate 0.1 not always met; historical partitions already exposed to prior research.

name: London Sweep Reversal
hypothesis: London open liquidity sweeps of the Asian range that close back inside tend to revert toward the opposite Asian boundary; the sweep extreme is structural invalidation.
entry_conditions: Executable pure detect(snapshot), causally replayed with completed supplied candles only.
exit_conditions: Fixed declared SL/TP and horizon from executable output; common frozen execution policy.
stop_loss_method: One planned risk unit; stop at sweep extreme plus 0.15 M15 ATR buffer; risk constrained to 0.6-5 ATR; no broker execution
take_profit_method: Structural target at opposite Asian boundary, admitted only at planned RR >= 2 (net gate intent)
risk_model: One planned risk unit; stop at sweep extreme plus 0.15 M15 ATR buffer; risk constrained to 0.6-5 ATR; no broker execution
intended_conditions: London open liquidity sweeps of the Asian range that close back inside tend to revert toward the opposite Asian boundary; the sweep extreme is structural invalidation.
limitations: No verified positive edge; session windows are UTC-fixed and ignore DST; CFD spread proxies; one opportunity per day; missing histories remain unresolved; tick volume is not centralized volume. Version history: 0.2.0: DST-aware London window (0.1.0 fixed UTC, one hour late in summer); sweep depth 0.05->0.10 ATR; rejection-wick confirmation added; Asian range cap 4.0->3.5 ATR.
